whatItDoes: Increase the Douglas County Board of Commissioners from three members to five. The ballot estimates an ongoing annual cost of $760,000 to $1.3 million, paid from county revenue that also supports public safety, transportation and other essential county services.
yesMeans: Approve expanding the county board to five members.
noMeans: Keep the board at three members.

whatItDoes: Choose an election method if Douglas County’s commission expands to five members. One option elects all five commissioners by district, with each commissioner living in the district and elected only by its voters. The other elects three district-resident commissioners only by voters in those districts, and two commissioners countywide. This is a choice between two methods, rather than a yes-or-no question. It applies only if the board expands.
If Douglas County’s board grows to five commissioners, continue having all registered county voters elect every commissioner, rather than limiting some or all seats to voters of individual districts.
yesMeans: Approve countywide voting for every commissioner if the board expands.
noMeans: Do not approve this requirement for countywide voting if the board expands.

whatItDoes: Require a Castle Pines voter election before annexing more than 20 acres owned or controlled by one owner or ownership group, or connected through a common development plan or related transactions. Related parcels annexed in single, successive, cumulative or simultaneous transactions would be combined when applying the rule.
yesMeans: Add the voter-approval requirement for these annexations to the city charter.
noMeans: Do not add this annexation requirement to the charter.

whatItDoes: Require a ratification election for annexation of a parcel over 20 acres owned or controlled by one owner or ownership group when annexed within 180 days of this charter section’s effective date. If no such annexation occurs in that 180-day period, the council could repeal the section by ordinance without a voter election.
yesMeans: Approve the annexation-ratification rule and the council’s conditional repeal authority.
noMeans: Do not add this rule to the city charter.

whatItDoes: Create a dedicated 0.129% Aurora sales and use tax from January 1, 2027 through December 31, 2057. It would raise up to $12.64 million initially and amounts based on collections annually afterward. Revenue would support operation, repair and improvement of libraries, recreation and community centers, and construction and renovation of parks, recreation centers and library branches. Authorize up to $105 million in revenue bonds, with total repayment capped at $204.87 million, paid from the new tax and other legally available funds. Tax revenue and investment earnings could be kept and spent despite limits in the Colorado Constitution, state law and the city charter.
yesMeans: Approve the dedicated sales and use tax, borrowing and revenue-limit exceptions.
noMeans: Do not authorize this tax, borrowing or the related revenue-limit exceptions.

whatItDoes: Create a dedicated 0.064% Aurora sales and use tax from January 1, 2027 through December 31, 2057. It would raise up to $6.27 million initially and amounts based on collections annually afterward. Revenue would support operation, repair and improvement of police, fire and other public-safety infrastructure and facilities, including fire stations, Aurora 911 and police facilities. Authorize up to $53 million in revenue bonds, with total repayment capped at $101.6 million, paid from the new tax and other legally available funds. Tax revenue and investment earnings could be kept and spent despite limits in the Colorado Constitution, state law and the city charter.
yesMeans: Approve the dedicated sales and use tax, borrowing and revenue-limit exceptions.
noMeans: Do not authorize this tax, borrowing or the related revenue-limit exceptions.

whatItDoes: Create a dedicated 0.132% Aurora sales and use tax from January 1, 2027 through December 31, 2057. It would raise up to $12.94 million initially and amounts based on collections annually afterward. Revenue would support operation, repair and improvement of transportation infrastructure and facilities, including traffic, intersection and pedestrian safety, bridge replacements, and roadway improvements and expansion. Authorize up to $108 million in revenue bonds, with total repayment capped at $209.733 million, paid from the new tax and other legally available funds. Tax revenue and investment earnings could be kept and spent despite limits in the Colorado Constitution, state law and the city charter.
yesMeans: Approve the dedicated sales and use tax, borrowing and revenue-limit exceptions.
noMeans: Do not authorize this tax, borrowing or the related revenue-limit exceptions.

whatItDoes: Move Aurora’s regular municipal elections from odd-numbered years to even-numbered years. Change the charter to allow one-time shorter terms of office needed for the transition.
yesMeans: Approve moving municipal elections to even-numbered years and the transition terms.
noMeans: Keep the existing election schedule and do not approve these transition changes.

whatItDoes: Increase Douglas County School District RE-1 property taxes by $54 million in 2026 for collection in 2027. Money would support general-fund purposes, including staff compensation, school security, career and technical education and restoring student programs such as elementary instrumental music. In later years, a property-tax levy combined with earlier voter-approved overrides could raise up to the district’s statutory limit. Tax revenue and investment earnings could be spent outside Colorado’s constitutional revenue limits and other legal limits. Spending would receive an annual independent audit posted online and oversight by a citizens’ committee.
yesMeans: Approve the additional education taxes, audit and citizen oversight, and revenue-limit exception.
noMeans: Do not approve this tax increase or its proposed revenue-limit exception.

whatItDoes: Add 3.97 mills to Larkspur Fire Protection District’s property-tax rate beginning January 1, 2027, raising $925,225 in the first full fiscal year and amounts based on collections later. Money would support fire and medical response, staffing, training, pay and benefits, accreditation, vehicles, facilities and equipment. Starting in tax collection year 2028, the district could adjust the levy to offset revenue losses from legislative changes, lower property values or other causes while accounting for growth, with annual review. District revenue could be collected, kept and spent despite legal revenue limits.
yesMeans: Approve the property-tax increase, later levy adjustments to maintain revenue and the revenue-limit exception.
noMeans: Do not approve this increase, adjustment authority or proposed revenue-limit exception.

whatItDoes: Authorize $4.5 million in Larkspur Fire Protection District debt, with total repayment capped at $6.4 million, and up to $427,333 in additional taxes annually to repay it. Projects include fire and emergency-medical vehicles and equipment, design and infrastructure for a future southeastern station, training grounds and simulators, and acquiring capital assets by prepaying existing leases. Debt could be general-obligation bonds or other multiyear obligations. Early repayment could include a premium of up to 3%. Tax revenue and investment earnings on taxes and bonds could be spent outside Colorado’s constitutional revenue limits and other legal limits.
yesMeans: Approve the capital debt, taxes to repay it and the revenue-limit exception.
noMeans: Do not authorize this borrowing, additional taxes or related revenue-limit exception.

whatItDoes: Immediately and permanently cancel all permission for Stone Creek Metropolitan District to borrow that voters approved in earlier elections but the district has not used.
yesMeans: Repeal the district’s unused debt authorizations.

whatItDoes: Immediately and permanently repeal Stone Creek’s 2014 Ballot Issue 5C. That measure authorizes multiyear financial obligations through intergovernmental agreements or contracts and property taxes of up to $1 million annually to fund them.
yesMeans: Repeal the 2014 authority for these multiyear obligations and related taxes.

whatItDoes: Immediately and permanently repeal Stone Creek’s 2014 Ballot Issue 5D. That measure authorizes multiyear financial obligations through agreements or contracts for regional improvements and property taxes of up to $1 million annually to fund them.
yesMeans: Repeal the 2014 authority for these regional-improvement obligations and related taxes.

whatItDoes: Immediately and permanently repeal Stone Creek’s 2014 Ballot Issue 5S. That measure allows intergovernmental agreements, which may create multiyear financial obligations, to jointly finance lawful public improvements and programs or district operations and maintenance.
yesMeans: Repeal this 2014 authority for intergovernmental financing agreements.

whatItDoes: Immediately and permanently repeal Stone Creek’s 2014 Ballot Issue 5T. That measure authorizes multiyear intergovernmental obligations for public improvements with regional authorities, other governments or government-owned enterprises. It permits up to $82.8 million in total district payments from property-tax revenue.
yesMeans: Repeal this 2014 authority for intergovernmental obligations and property-tax-funded payments.
